data.gender_notes: Rowland is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Old English Hroðwulf, composed of the elements hroth (fame, glory, wealth) and wulf (wolf). The name Rowland was popular among the Anglo-Saxons and Normans, as a strong and courageous name for a warrior or nobleman. The name Rowland carries the meaning “Brave as a wolf” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Rowland usually hope their child will grow to embody brave as a wolf and live with faith, good character and purpose.
